function: Channel estimation from underdetermined pilots by annealed higher-order Langevin sampling with a learned score-network prior (p. 9); detection experiment uses a closed-form prior, not learned (p. 8).
system: MIMO: base station with Nr=16 antennas, Nu=64 single-antenna users, pilots Np=0.6Nu, CDL-C channel; no RIS; frequency band not stated (p. 9).
method: Score network (architecture of [57]) trained unsupervised by denoising score matching as in [16], used as prior in annealed underdamped and third-order Langevin sampling (p. 6, 9).
data_channel: Standardized 3GPP CDL-C channel model (TR 38.901) with Nu=64, Nr=16 for channel estimation; score network trained as in [16]; detection uses simulated Kronecker Rayleigh (p. 7-9, 14).
test_conditions: Channel model CDL-C, Nu=64, Nr=16, 0.6Nu pilots; score network trained as in [16]; NMSE tested over SNR -10 to 20 dB; no other scenario tested (p. 9-11).
baselines: Channel estimation: Lasso and fsAD (classical), L-DAMP (learned unrolling), overdamped Langevin of [16] (learned score); detection: MMSE, V-BLAST, SDR, ML, RE-MIMO, OAMPNet (p. 7, 9).
metrics: NMSE versus SNR for channel estimation; SER and running time (ms/symbol) for detection; PSNR, LPIPS, FID, SSIM for images (p. 7-12, 19).
complexity: Detection: O(NuNr*min{Nu,Nr}+LT(Nu^2+K*Nu)) and runtime in ms/symb (p. 8); channel estimation: only iterations (L=58 vs 2311), cost tied to score network [16] (p. 9-10).
q1_support: p. 9: "we use the standardized clustered delay line (CDL)-C model, which is adopted in 5G specifications" - reference [56] is 3GPP TR 38.901 (p. 14); score-network training is only described by reference to [16].
q2_support: p. 9: "We consider Nu = 64 and Nr = 16" - one CDL-C setting and an SNR sweep for channel estimation; no unseen scenario, band, or antenna count is tested for the learned model.
q3_support: p. 9: "Lasso [50]: This is a compressive-sensing-based approach" (non-learned) and "This method is a data-driven algorithm that uses algorithm unrolling" (L-DAMP, learned); p. 10: "our proposed methods outperform the other baselines for SNRs greater than 0 dB" (NMSE, Fig. 2c).
q4_support: p. 8: "the overall complexity, including the SVD computation and all the iterations" is given as an order, and "running time in ms/symb" is measured; both for the detection experiment, while channel estimation gives iteration counts only (p. 9).
q5_support: p. 7: "Code to replicate the numerical experiments can be found at" https://github.com/nzilberstein/higher-order-langevin (footnote 2).
notes: Included, area 2: the learned element is the score network of the channel-estimation experiment (denoising score matching, as in [16]); the MIMO-detection experiment (area 1) uses a closed-form prior and is not learned; image experiments are outside the scope. q1 rests on the declared CDL-C model, the training data being described only by reference to [16]. q4 rests on the detection experiment; channel estimation gives iteration counts only.
